## Summary

```text
settings: Title → FPS → Quality → … → Back (updated y<200)
hotkeys: Title → … → Pause (updated y<400)
                           ├ Back
                           └ Locked
```

Add the settings/hotkey geometry importer and frame model before connecting the screen. Persistence, bindings and UI remain separate backlog changes.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no model of the authored staggered row motion.
  **After:** tests preserve quantized same-frame gates, retained exits and freeze behavior. At hotkey frame36, Pause reaches398.8 and Back/Locked independently move to543.85/539.35.
- Independent ActionScript/pcode audit confirms formulas, order and source-state mapping. The caller must freeze Info/closing and reset hotkey return state on new entry; this layer does not claim the complete state machine.
- Two repeatable imports match backlog data byte for byte (SHA2561d24479e701061f502ed1d136c9ef91725c6bfa2a08450e78b89205eb4bd6b77). Relevant root/frame placements agree with the shared parser; origins verified against pause placements and menu source.
- Formatting, TypeScript,444 tests /5705 assertions and production build pass. Visible browser flows are unchanged. No SWF, original images/audio or vector outlines are committed.
- Original settings recordings, final caller routing, text/filter pixels and complete-game parity remain unverified.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** model

Geometry contains numeric placements/bounds plus label and field/font metadata. Screen integration follows separately.

payload.diffStr:
@@ -543 +543,9 @@
 - Formatting, TypeScript,444 rule/parser tests with5705 assertions and production build pass. This adds no visible browser flow; persistence/key binding and UI integration follow separately. Controlled original settings recordings, browser text/filter rasterization, source state routing in the final caller and complete-game parity remain unverified.
+
+### Flash logical keys and input latches
+
+- `_‑Ay.as:44–188,205–212` captures received numeric key codes without rejecting duplicates. `hotkeys.ts` maps supported browser codes to that logical domain, preserves the source punctuation/numpad labels and its unretained `toUpperCase()` return: F1 displays lowercase `p`. Profile validation now accepts the supported codes and canonicalizes modifier/Enter aliases. The full settings picker and frame-rate/session changes remain separate backlog work.
+- `AvatarInterface.as:519–533,558–567,675–727` keeps unique logical key codes and removes a code on keyup. Its Up/else-Down and independent Left/else-Right chains give Up/Left priority for same-axis duplicate bindings while permitting a shared key across axes. Space assigned horizontally cannot start secondary fire; vertical Space still can. If secondary was already latched, changing Space to horizontal while held leaves it latched until release. The browser controller now preserves those contracts and suppresses browser defaults for bound keys.
+- Source lines729–733 sample the lock key once per frame with `blnHoldHot6`. The backlog’s event-based callback incorrectly fired twice when two physical modifier keys mapped to one logical code. `GameInput.frame()` now owns the held-key edge; a key pressed and released between sampled frames triggers no lock callback. Dialog shortcut handling uses the same canonical code, preserving layout-effect focus transfer and permitting either modifier alias to resume a paused game. The base offline game still has no lock registration target.
+- A development-only fixture drives the production profile validator and `GameInput` with real keyboard events. It covers aliases/release, duplicate priorities, Space latch changes, lock edges and clearing; a second case exercises an actual game pause/resume through the production dialog. The initial new game test sent its key while only the application container existed; it now waits for the initialized renderer canvas. No product delay or sleep was added.
+- Limits remain: browser physical-code versus Flash numeric-code translation depends on keyboard layout/platform, and the browser adapter supports a bounded code list rather than arbitrary Flash numbers. Original insertion-order movement/clamping, general event ordering and native keyboard comparison still need verification. These changes do not establish complete-game parity.
